about: Tool-selection labels for the 71 benchmark items, used by eval/tool_metrics.py. A sidecar file on purpose: it is NOT part of benchmark_version (eval/experiment.py hashes benchmark.csv and the chunk labels only), so adding or revising it never orphans a committed results file; tool_metrics records this file's sha256 instead.

fields.first_tool_ok: tools acceptable as the first call (rule 7: lookup_financial_fact first for a tagged headline figure; search_filings first for narrative, cover-page and untagged items)
fields.allowed_tools: any tool outside this set is a selection error
fields.required_tools: tools that must appear (compute_metric where the question asks for a growth rate, change or difference: rule 8)
fields.tickers: the companies the item concerns; a lookup for any other ticker is an argument error
fields.fiscal_year: the year the question names (the later one when it names two), else null
fields.fiscal_years_ok: optional; every year a lookup may legitimately pass (adds the base year of a growth question). Absent means [fiscal_year] when that is not null

audit.method: After the labels above were written and before any results file was opened, three independent labellers (subagents given only the benchmark question, ground truth, question_type and section, the prompt rules 5-8 and the tool docstrings) labelled all 71 items from scratch. They agreed with the author's first_tool_ok on 65, 64 and 61 of 71 items, allowed_tools on 61, 56 and 62, required_tools on 71, 71 and 71, and fiscal_year on 70, 71 and 71.
audit.adjudication: Widened (a defensible alternative named by 2 or 3 of 3, or a tagged cover/segment fact): qa_0001 and qa_0048 first_tool_ok and allowed_tools gain lookup_financial_fact; allowed_tools gains lookup_financial_fact on qa_0003, qa_0016, qa_0023, qa_0028, qa_0040, qa_0051. Narrowed (all three found a fact lookup indefensible): qa_0013, qa_0045, qa_0050 lose lookup_financial_fact from allowed_tools. Left as written where the author's set was already the wider one (qa_0044, qa_0060 to qa_0063, qa_0069) or one labeller of three dissented (search as a first call on the growth questions qa_0021, qa_0041, qa_0053, where rule 7 is explicit).
audit.independence: The panel is not independent of the author in the way a human annotator would be: all four are language models reading the same rules (eval/EVALUATION.md, "Tool-call quality", limits).

owner_review.when: after the results files of contract-v3, reindex-v3, upgrade-control and upgrade-v1 had been read; post hoc, unlike the 2026-10-04 adjudication
owner_review.rule: list_available_companies is an acceptable first call, and an allowed tool, on an item whose question names no company: the ticker a lookup needs must be inferred from a product or segment name, and the tool's docstring sanctions confirming availability first. On an item that names its company the orientation call stays a selection error.

kept.qa_0008, qa_0029, qa_0038, qa_0065: the question names the company; the first list_available_companies call was unneeded
kept.qa_0034: compute_metric stays required by the field's definition (a difference, rule 8). In upgrade-control the $26.4 billion difference was retrieved verbatim from MD&A after two lookups found nothing, so the miss is a rule-8 conformity miss, not arithmetic in the model's head.

owner_review.applied_to: every item meeting the condition, not only the misses: qa_0019 and qa_0020 were already passing in every committed run
owner_review.effect: first_tool_ok / tool_set_ok of 71: contract-v3 67/67 to 69/69, reindex-v3 67/66 to 69/68, upgrade-control 65/64 to 67/66, upgrade-v1 70/69 unchanged; call validity unchanged in every file
